info.title: Annotation Platform
info.description:
## Maven Annotation Platform API

Full REST API for the Maven annotation platform.

### Authentication

All protected endpoints accept **either** of the following:

#### 1. JWT Bearer Token (login-based)
Obtain a token via `POST /api/auth/login`, then pass it as:
```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

#### 2. API Key (programmatic access)
Generate a key via `POST /api/auth/api-key` (admin/pm only), then pass it as:
```
X-API-Key: apk_<your-key>
```

API keys are available to users with the **admin** or **pm** role.
They can be generated and revoked from the admin UI under **🔑 API Key**.

Permanently wipe a user and ALL their associated data from the database (admin only).

This is irreversible. The following data is deleted in order:
  - Session replays, behavior events, annotation traces, AI detections
  - Speed trap results
  - Scoring events, QA reviews, gold encounters
  - Qualification statuses, project limits, quality daily, project confidences
  - Assignments (and their submissions via cascade)
  - Team memberships
  - The user record itself

Projects created by this user have their created_by field set to NULL.

When SMTP is configured the link is emailed; otherwise it is
printed to the server log (useful in local dev).

the supplied address is syntactically valid, registered, or active —

The schema accepts a plain str (not EmailStr) so that Pydantic's
pre-handler validation does not produce a distinguishable 422 for
malformed addresses.  A minimal @ check is performed here instead,
silently discarding obviously invalid input without leaking information.

post.description:
Clone a project, its configuration, teams, tasks, and (optionally) data.

Creates a new project that is an exact copy of the source project's
configuration fields (type, applet, QA policy, work limits, collection
config, telephony config, etc.). The new project gets:
  - name prefixed with "Copy of "
  - status reset to "active"
  - a fresh id / created_at
  - S3 config IS copied so the clone can immediately store/read artifacts
    (e.g. telephony recordings). Credentials inside ``s3_config`` are
    already stored encrypted, so copying the blob does not re-expose them.

Controlled by :class:`CloneProjectRequest` (all default on):
  - ``include_team_assignments`` — copy ``project_teams`` so the clone's
    access rules resolve to the same annotators immediately.
  - ``include_tasks`` — copy every task with its full config (allow/forbid
    lists, QA, qualification, replication, time caps). Intra-project
    ``qualification_task_id`` references are remapped to the cloned tasks.
  - ``include_units`` — copy each task's units (the input data) as a fresh,
    unworked queue. Requires ``include_tasks``. Assignments/submissions/
    scoring are never copied.

patch.description: Apply only changed caps while preserving concurrent bulk-cap updates.

Apply one individual project cap to every current member of a team.

Individual limits are deliberately kept in the project's existing
``user_work_limits`` map, rather than introducing a competing per-team
limit model. A cap of zero removes the individual limit for each member.
The project row is locked so this bulk operation is atomic.

Members added later inherit that established per-person cap from their
teammates (see ``inherit_established_user_work_limits``). Existing
per-member overrides are left untouched at add time.

get.description:
Unified per-annotator quality data for a project, powering the Quality Control
tab's single actionable table.

For each annotator who has a qualification status, a confidence score, or any
gold-unit encounter in the project, returns:
  * project-level qualification status (the gate) + progress/accuracy/failures
  * project-level confidence score + blacklist action
  * an ``overall`` gold-encounter aggregate (all tasks)
  * a ``by_task`` breakdown so the UI can re-scope accuracy/failures to one task

The UI does search / sort / filter / pagination client-side (annotator counts
per project are small), and switches the displayed accuracy/failure figures to
the ``by_task`` entry when a task filter is applied. Failure *details* (answers
vs. gold) are fetched lazily per annotator via the ``/failures`` endpoint.

Failure drill-down: a user's gold-unit encounters (failed by default), enriched
with their answer, the correct answer, and the per-field breakdown — so a PM can
see *what* an annotator got wrong. Optionally scoped to a single task.

post.description:
Skip the currently claimed unit (annotation or QA).

Releases the claim (marks it as 'skipped') so the user can claim the next unit.
The unit remains in the queue and will be served again once the reviewer
has exhausted all other available units.

Import units for a task

Accepts a list of unit payloads and creates units in the database

Claim next available unit for annotation or QA

Uses FCFS with database locking to prevent double-claiming

Claim a specific unit for annotation/QA via a share link token.

Validates the share token, verifies it matches the requested unit_id and
is intended for the current user, then creates an assignment (or returns
an existing active one).

Send heartbeat to keep claim alive and track time.

When the heartbeat fails, we look at the assignment state to determine
*why* it failed:

- state == 'abandoned' → an administrator released the claim (for example,
  through a unit reset). We return a 409 with detail
  "UNIT_RESET_BY_ADMIN" so the annotator UI can show a clear, friendly
  message.
- Otherwise (TTL expiry, cross-task expiry, invalid token, deleted
  assignment) → 400 as before. Note: unit.status cannot be used to detect
  a reset — it is a QA-lifecycle status that stays 'open' for the whole
  annotation phase, so it matches every expired claim, not just resets.

Submit completed annotation or QA.

Optionally accepts a `behavior_events` array in the request body —
behaviour telemetry collected by the Annotator SPA.  These are
processed asynchronously (BackgroundTask) so they never add latency.

Re-presign a claimed unit's S3-backed assets.

Fixes mid-unit 403s on long-running units: the presigned URLs handed to the
applet at claim time expire, but the applet has no AWS credentials to
re-sign them itself. The shell calls this endpoint on behalf of the applet
(on manual reload, before opening an at-risk-age document, or on a proactive
timer) and forwards the result back into the iframe as `ASSETS_REFRESHED`.

Only re-signs objects that already appear as s3:// paths somewhere in the
unit's payload_json, and only while the caller holds the assignment's
current claim — `asset_keys` is intersected against that set, never signed
verbatim. Rate-limited to 1 request / 10s / assignment (RATE-006); the
shell is expected to debounce further on top of this.

Import units from CSV file

CSV should have headers. Each row becomes a unit payload.
Special columns:
- external_key: optional stable ID
- unit_type: 'normal' or 'gold'
- gold_json: JSON string for gold truth
- gold_policy_json: JSON string for legacy gold scoring policy
- gold_type: 'feedback' or 'testing'
- gold_answers_json: JSON string for v2 golden answers
- gold_comment: optional admin notes
- payload_json: optional JSON object for the full unit payload

Import **multi-turn** (conversation) units from CSV or JSONL.

One conversation → one unit whose ``payload_json`` carries a ``turns`` array.

Supported inputs (auto-detected by content / filename):

- **CSV (one row per turn)** — rows are grouped by ``conversation_id``
  (aliases: ``conversation_key``), ordered by ``turn_index`` (aliases:
  ``turn``, ``turn_number``). Every other column becomes a field on that
  turn object (e.g. ``role``, ``text``, ``speaker``, ``audio_url``).
  Conversation-level fields use the ``_conv_`` prefix (``_conv_context`` →
  ``payload.context``). Reserved unit keys (``_external_key``, ``_unit_type``,
  ``_gold_*``) may appear on any row and are lifted to the unit.

- **JSONL / JSON array (one object per conversation)** — each object is a
  unit; put the turns inline under ``turns``. Reserved ``_*`` keys behave
  exactly as in the standard ``/units/import`` endpoint.

Example CSV::

    conversation_id,turn_index,role,text,_conv_context
    c1,0,user,I want to fly to Rome,Booking a flight
    c1,1,assistant,When would you like to go?,
    c2,0,user,Cancel my booking,Support call

Example JSONL::

    {"_external_key":"c1","context":"Booking","turns":[{"turn_index":0,"role":"user","text":"Hi"}]}

Bulk-mark units as golden.

Each item must supply either unit_id (UUID) or external_key.
gold_answers supports the v2 per-key structured format:
  { "label": {"value": "positive", "match": "exact"}, ... }
or a plain dict (treated as exact-match gold answers).

Save partial applet output as a draft without submitting.

Requires the project to have ``draft_save_enabled`` turned on. When it is
off this returns 409 DRAFT_SAVE_DISABLED — the annotator gates its autosave
loop on the same flag (delivered in the claim response), so a well-behaved
client never calls this; the check exists so a stale tab or a custom applet
firing SAVE_DRAFT cannot reintroduce the write load the flag is meant to
remove.

Body:
  claim_token   – must match the active claim
  output_json   – current applet state (any JSON object)
  active_time_ms – accumulated active (non-idle) time so far

Manually queue units for QA review.

Units must have at least one annotation submission (status = 'submitted').
Units already in QA (qa_override=True, qa_in_progress, or qa_reviewed) are skipped
unless they have no pending QA assignment.

Resend already-reviewed units back to QA for a second review.

Unlike send-to-qa, this endpoint accepts units that already have QA submissions.
It sets qa_override=True so the unit re-enters the QA queue.

Granularity: resend is unit-level and re-queues **every** annotation
submission on the unit. ``qa_resend_count`` is raised strictly above the
highest per-submission completed-QA count so each replica satisfies
``qa_resend_count > completed_qa_for_that_submission``.

Remove units from the QA queue — the inverse of send-to-qa. Clears
``qa_override`` so routed-but-unreviewed units return to the 'submitted'
state (e.g. undoing an over-eager LLM judge that routed a batch).

Provide ``unit_ids`` for a specific selection, or set ``all=True`` to remove
every routed unit in the task. Units with an active (claimed) QA review, or
that already have a completed QA review, are skipped so no in-flight or
finished QA work is ever discarded.

Route a random percentage of submitted units to QA.

Selects a random sample of units that are in 'submitted' status
(have annotation submissions, no QA submissions, not already queued)
and sets qa_override=True on them.

This is the "after-the-fact routing" endpoint — useful when you want to
retroactively send e.g. 10% of already-submitted work through QA.

Reset (release) units so they re-enter the claim pool.

By default this only releases *active* (non-submitted) claims — both
annotation and QA — by marking them ``state='abandoned'`` and clearing
their draft (``draft_output_json`` / ``draft_saved_at``). This is the
safe "stuck / reassign" path.

If ``include_submitted`` is true, already-submitted assignments for the
selected units are also released (marked ``abandoned``) so the unit can be
re-worked. The underlying ``Submission`` rows are **preserved** for the
record — only the assignment state changes.

Reset QA so selected units are pending QA again — including units that
have already completed QA (the primary operator case).

"Pending QA" in this codebase means the unit is eligible for a QA claim:
no live assignment in ``submitted`` or unexpired ``claimed`` state that
still counts as QA-done, and either sampled by the task QA policy or
``qa_override=True``. Completed QA assignments are marked ``abandoned``
(Submission rows stay for audit). ``QAReview`` verdicts are set to
``superseded``. ``qa_resend_count`` is raised above the completed-QA
count so claiming cannot treat the unit as already done.

post.description:
Import QA feedback from CSV. Creates or updates QAReview records for
annotator submissions.

Two modes:
  - Default (`feedback_only=False`): the previous behavior. Each row must
    carry a `verdict` and a new QAReview is created. Rows whose annotation
    already has a QAReview are rejected.
  - `feedback_only=True`: never write to verdict or score. For each row the
    endpoint either updates the existing QAReview's
    `issues_json.feedback_comment` / `internal_comment` in place, or creates
    a feedback-only review (`verdict=null`, `score=null`) when none exists.
    Verdict columns are ignored if present.

On a per-row basis, an empty `verdict` cell in default mode is also treated
as feedback-only for that row, so mixed CSVs behave sensibly.

CSV columns:
  - `unit_id` OR `external_key` (at least one required)
  - `verdict` (required in default mode unless the row leaves it blank)
  - `score` 0.0-1.0 (optional; derived from verdict when missing)
  - `feedback_comment` (visible to the annotator)
  - `internal_comment` (admin/PM only)

Move or copy units to a different task (which may be in a different project).

Modes:
  - **move**: Reassigns the unit's task_id to the target task. Active claims
    and assignments are abandoned. Submissions are preserved for audit but
    the unit starts fresh in the new task.
  - **copy**: Creates a duplicate of the unit (new UUID) in the target task.
